from.place: Second paragraph, final warning: Closedness of T^c is a separate condition; it does not follow from uniqueness of closed specializations.

title: Unique closed specializations do not force closed closed-point locus
statement: There exists a spectral topological space $T$ [def-weil-spectral-space] such that, writing $T^c=\{c\in T:\{c\}\text{ is closed}\}$, for each $x\in T$ there is exactly one $c\in T^c$ with $c\in\overline{\{x\}}$, but $T^c$ is not closed in $T$.
